El salitre sí tenía propiedades que dificultaban la concepción, así que el remedio no era pura superstición.
detail.en: The Kahun Papyrus, from around 1850 BC, contains the oldest known written description of a contraceptive: a suppository of crocodile dung, saltpeter, and fermented dough. The saltpeter did have properties that hindered conception, so the remedy wasn't pure superstition.

source: World History Encyclopedia — Family Planning in the Ancient Near East
_evidence: Egyptian physicians recommended preparing a suppository combining crocodile dung, saltpeter, and fermented dough... the saltpeter could block conception.

question.es: ¿Tuvo Londres una línea de tren dedicada en exclusiva a transportar cadáveres fuera de la ciudad?
question.en: Did London have a train line dedicated solely to carrying corpses out of the city?

answer.es: Sí, durante 87 años: los cementerios estaban tan saturados que hacía falta sacar a los muertos en tren.
answer.en: Yes, for 87 years: the cemeteries were so overcrowded that the dead had to be shipped out by train.

detail.es: Tras una epidemia de cólera que dejó más de 14.000 muertos sin sitio donde enterrarlos, se abrió en 1854 un cementerio a 37 km de Londres y un tren propio que salía de Waterloo con ataúdes y familiares en duelo el mismo día. Una bomba destruyó su estación de salida en un bombardeo de 1941 y el servicio nunca volvió a funcionar.
detail.en: After a cholera epidemic left over 14,000 dead with nowhere to be buried, a cemetery opened in 1854 some 23 miles from London along with its own train that left Waterloo carrying coffins and grieving families the same day. A 1941 bombing destroyed its departure station, and the service never ran again.

source: National Geographic — The history of the London Necropolis Railway
_evidence: with 14,601 people dying and no burial space for the influx of corpses... the 1941 bombing of Waterloo Station led to the permanent closure of the venture.

question.es: ¿Por qué una «docena de panadero» son en realidad trece panes y no doce?
question.en: Why is a "baker's dozen" actually thirteen loaves, not twelve?

answer.es: Por miedo: una ley medieval castigaba con multa, cepo o cárcel vender pan que pesara de menos.
answer.en: Out of fear: a medieval law punished selling underweight bread with fines, the stocks, or jail.

detail.es: Desde 1266, una ley inglesa fijaba el peso exacto que debía tener cada pan, pero la levadura hacía que dos panes iguales pesaran distinto de forma impredecible. Para no arriesgarse a una condena por un gramo de menos, los panaderos añadían un pan de propina a cada docena vendida, como colchón de seguridad.
detail.en: From 1266, an English law fixed the exact weight each loaf had to be, but yeast made two identical-looking loaves weigh differently in unpredictable ways. Rather than risk punishment over a few missing grams, bakers threw in one extra loaf with every dozen sold, as a safety cushion.

source: Tasting Table — The Medieval History Behind A Baker's Dozen
_evidence: Any baker caught violating the laws associated with this body would be subject to fines, beatings, or even imprisonment... an extra (typically smaller) loaf or end piece of bread as insurance.

question.es: ¿Por qué el día después de Navidad se llama «Boxing Day» en países de habla inglesa?
question.en: Why is the day after Christmas called "Boxing Day" in English-speaking countries?

answer.es: Por las cajas de regalos que los señores entregaban ese día a sus criados y proveedores.
answer.en: Because of the boxes of gifts masters handed out that day to their servants and tradesmen.

detail.es: El servicio trabajaba el día de Navidad para que sus señores pudieran celebrar, así que recibía su propio día libre y su caja de regalo justo después. Otra teoría, no excluyente, lo liga a las cajas de limosna de las iglesias, que se abrían ese mismo día para repartir donativos entre los pobres.
detail.en: Servants worked on Christmas Day so their employers could celebrate, so they got their own day off and their gift box right after. Another, not mutually exclusive, theory ties it to church alms boxes, which were opened that same day to distribute donations to the poor.

source: Britannica — Boxing Day
_evidence: it came from the boxes of gifts given to employees on the day after Christmas... it derived from the opening of alms boxes that had been placed in churches for the collection of donations to aid the poor.

question.es: ¿Se cazaban ballenas hasta casi extinguirlas sobre todo para fabricar corsés de moda?
question.en: Were whales hunted nearly to extinction mainly to make fashionable corsets?

answer.es: No: durante el siglo XVIII el motivo principal era el aceite, no las varillas de las faldas.
answer.en: No: through the 18th century the main reason was oil, not skirt hoops.

detail.es: Las barbas de ballena, mal llamadas «huesos», sí armaban corsés y miriñaques, pero eran un producto secundario rentable, no la razón de cazar. El verdadero motor era el aceite de ballena, usado para iluminar, lubricar máquinas y fabricar jabón; solo a finales del XIX, cuando el petróleo sustituyó ese aceite, las barbas pasaron a ser el objetivo principal de la caza.
detail.en: Whale baleen, misleadingly called "whalebone," really did frame corsets and hoop skirts, but it was a profitable side product, not the reason for hunting. The real driver was whale oil, used for lighting, machine lubrication, and soap; only in the late 19th century, once petroleum replaced that oil, did baleen become the main target of the hunt.

source: The Conversation — 'Whales died so women could look like this': what Bridgerton gets wrong about whalebone
_evidence: fashion was not the driving motivator for whaling during the 18th century... It was not until the late 19th century, when petroleum products replaced the need for oil, that whales were killed primarily for their baleen.

question.es: ¿Se puede ser rey de un país durante solo veinte minutos?
question.en: Can someone be king of a country for just twenty minutes?

answer.es: Sí: Luis XIX de Francia heredó la corona y renunció a ella veinte minutos después, en 1830.
answer.en: Yes: Louis XIX of France inherited the crown and gave it up twenty minutes later, in 1830.

detail.es: En plena Revolución de Julio, su padre Carlos X firmó la abdicación y le cedió el trono; Luis Antonio firmó su propia renuncia en el mismo documento apenas veinte minutos después, sin llegar a ejercer ni un solo acto de gobierno. Algunos monárquicos siguieron considerándolo el legítimo rey de Francia el resto de su vida.
detail.en: In the middle of the July Revolution, his father Charles X signed his abdication and passed him the throne; Louis Antoine signed his own renunciation on the very same document barely twenty minutes later, without ever performing a single act of government. Some monarchists kept considering him the rightful king of France for the rest of his life.

source: History Facts — The shortest reign of any monarch lasted just 20 minutes

question.es: ¿Alcanzó un papa a dejar alguna huella en la Iglesia habiendo reinado solo trece días?
question.en: Did a pope manage to leave a mark on the Church despite reigning only thirteen days?

answer.es: Sí: murió de malaria antes de coronarse, pero antes decretó la primera prohibición de fumar.
answer.en: Yes: he died of malaria before his coronation, but not before decreeing the first-ever smoking ban.

detail.es: Urbano VII fue elegido papa el 15 de septiembre de 1590 y murió el día 27, sin llegar a coronarse: el pontificado más corto de la historia de la Iglesia. En esos pocos días prohibió fumar tabaco dentro o cerca de las iglesias, bajo pena de excomunión, mucho antes de que nadie supiera nada sobre los riesgos del tabaco para la salud.
detail.en: Urban VII was elected pope on September 15, 1590 and died on the 27th, without ever being crowned: the shortest papacy in Church history. In those few days he banned smoking tobacco in or near churches, on pain of excommunication, long before anyone knew anything about the health risks of tobacco.

source: Aleteia — 5 Shortest papacies in history, even shorter than John Paul I
_evidence: holds the record for the shortest papacy, lasting just 13 days before dying of malaria... introducing what is considered the world's first public smoking ban, forbidding tobacco use in or near churches under threat of excommunication.
